source: NCERT Class IX, Contemporary India I, Geography Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Drainage Basics
points: **Drainage** = the river system of an area; the area drained by a river and its tributaries = a **drainage basin**.
A ridge separating two drainage basins = a **water divide** (e.g. the Ambala water divide; the Western Ghats).
Indian rivers fall into two groups: **Himalayan** and **Peninsular**.

sections.heading: 2. Himalayan Rivers
points: **Perennial** (fed by snow-melt and rain); do **erosion**, form **meanders, ox-bow lakes and large deltas**.

sub: **Indus** — rises in Tibet; tributaries **Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej**.
**Ganga** — from **Gangotri (Bhagirathi)**; joined by Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi (left) and Son (right); forms the **Sundarban delta** with the Brahmaputra.
**Brahmaputra** — rises in Tibet (as **Tsangpo**); enters India in Arunachal (**Dihang**); huge water, braided channels, floods.

sections.heading: 3. Peninsular Rivers
points: Mostly **seasonal (rain-fed)**; shorter, shallower.
**East-flowing** (into the **Bay of Bengal**, form deltas): **Mahanadi, Godavari (the 'Dakshin Ganga', largest peninsular river), Krishna, Kaveri**.
**West-flowing** (into the **Arabian Sea**, form **estuaries**): **Narmada** (flows in a rift valley; Marble Rocks) and **Tapi**.
The main water divide is the **Western Ghats**.

sections.heading: 4. Lakes and River Importance
points: **Freshwater lakes** (Himalayan, e.g. **Wular** — largest freshwater lake in India, formed by tectonics; Dal); **lagoons/saltwater** (**Chilika** — Odisha, largest lagoon; Pulicat).
**Sambhar** (Rajasthan) is a salt lake.
Rivers are vital for **water, irrigation, hydropower, navigation** — but suffer **pollution** (e.g. Ganga → **Namami Gange** programme).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Drainage basin = area drained by a river; water divide = ridge between basins.
Himalayan rivers = perennial (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra); Peninsular = seasonal.
Indus tributaries: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej; Ganga from Gangotri; Brahmaputra = Tsangpo/Dihang.
Godavari = 'Dakshin Ganga' (largest peninsular river); Narmada & Tapi flow west (estuaries).
Wular = largest freshwater lake; Chilika = largest lagoon; Sambhar = salt lake.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Narmada and Tapi** flow **west** into the Arabian Sea (estuaries); most peninsular rivers flow **east** (deltas).
**Godavari** is the **largest peninsular river** ('Dakshin Ganga').
**Brahmaputra** = Tsangpo (Tibet) → Dihang (Arunachal).
**Wular** = largest freshwater lake; **Chilika** = largest coastal lagoon (Odisha).
